source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: These{H428} are the generations{H8435} of Yeshua{H3442}, son{H1121} of David{H1732}, son of Avraham{H85}.

one_way_hebrew: אלה תולדות — the Torah's own structuring formula (Gen 2:4; 6:9; 11:27; 37:2), and זה ספר תולדת of Gen 5:1. The book opens exactly as the Torah's generation-lists open; Greek Βίβλος γενέσεως is a translation of this formula.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ראשון (Perek 1) begins here.

The ms writes the name as יש״ו throughout — an abbreviation marked with gershayim. At 1:21 and 1:25, where the naming itself and the wordplay יושיע ('he will save') are explicit, the ms writes the name out: ישו״ע (see 1:21).
Howard's apparatus (1:1): בן דוד omitted in C.

verses.translation: Avraham{H85} begot{H3205} Yitschaq{H3327}, and Yitschaq begot Yaakov{H3290}; Yaakov begot Yehudah{H3063} and his brothers{H251}.

one_way_hebrew: הוליד את — the hiphil begetting-formula of Gen 5, Gen 11, Ruth 4:18-22, and 1 Chr 1-3 (הוליד את), the Chronicler's own list-style. Greek ἐγέννησεν translates it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:2): ויצחק] יצחק DEFG; יהודה] יודא BEF (the Aramaic-type short form; cf. 24:16).

verses.translation: Yehudah{H3063} begot{H3205} Perets{H6557} and Zerach{H2226} from Tamar{H8559}; Perets begot Chetsron{H2696}; Chetsron begot Ram{H7410}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:3): יהודה] יודא BDEFG; the second חצרון] וחצרון EF.

verses.translation: And Ram{H7410} begot{H3205} Amminadav{H5992}; and Amminadav begot Nachshon{H5177}; and Nachshon begot Salmon{H8012}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:4): ורם] רם ABDG; ועמינדב] עמינדב ABDG; ונחשון] נחשון ABDG; שלמון omitted in A.

verses.translation: Salmon{H8012} begot{H3205} Boaz{H1162} from Rachav{H7343} the harlot{H2181}; Boaz begot Oved{H5744} from Rut{H7327}; and Oved begot Yishai{H3448}.

one_way_hebrew: רחב הזונה — Joshua's own designation, letter for letter (Josh 6:25, רחב הזונה): the base text names her as the book of Joshua names her. Greek has only 'Rachab.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:5): הזונה omitted in ABDEFG — only the base ms keeps Joshua's epithet; שלמון הוליד את omitted in A; ועובד] עובד ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: Yishai{H3448} begot{H3205} David{H1732}; David begot Shlomo{H8010} from the wife{H802} of Uriyah{H223}.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew lacks 'David THE KING' (Greek τὸν Δαυὶδ τὸν βασιλέα); only ms A adds המלך.
translation_notes: The base ms reads את אשת שלמה — literally 'the wife of Shlomo' — the copyist's eye caught by מאשת אוריה just ahead; mss ABCDG read את שלמה, and Howard prints '(Solomon)' in parentheses. The translation follows the sense; the words preserve the ms.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:6): את אשת שלמה] את שלמה ABCDG; מאשת] מבת שבע אשת F ('from Bathsheba, wife of Uriah'); דוד] + המלך A.

verses.translation: Shlomo{H8010} begot{H3205} Rechavam{H7346}; Rechavam begot Aviyah{H29}; Aviyah begot Asa{H609}.
Asa{H609} begot{H3205} Yehoshafat{H3092}; Yehoshafat begot Yoram{H3141}; Yoram begot Uzziyah{H5818}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:8): עוזיה] עזיהו EF; the second יורם] ויורם B; יהושפט] יושפט EF.

verses.translation: Uzziyah{H5818} begot{H3205} Chizqiyah{H2396}.

greek_deviations: The base text passes straight from Uzziah to Hezekiah, omitting Jotham and Ahaz (Greek Matthew: Uzziah–Jotham–Ahaz–Hezekiah). Mss ADG supply יותם הוליד את אחז אחז הוליד את, and Howard prints '(Jotham, Jotham begot Ahaz, Ahaz begot)' in parentheses. Greek Matthew itself drops three kings (Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah) between Joram and Uzziah to force the fourteen-count; the base Hebrew list is shorter still — and carries no fourteen-count at all (see v. 17).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:9): את] + יותם הוליד את אחז אחז הוליד את ADG.

verses.translation: Chizqiyah{H2396} begot{H3205} Menasheh{H4519}; Menasheh begot Amon{H526}; Amon begot Yoshiyah{H2977}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:10): the first את omitted in EF; the second את] + יושיהו G; יאשיה] יאשיא A, יאשיהו EF.

verses.translation: Yoshiyah{H2977} begot{H3205} Yekhonyah{H3204} and his brothers{H251} in the exile{H1546} of Bavel{H894}.

one_way_hebrew: גלות בבל — 'the exile of Bavel': galut, the Hebrew word that still names the experience (2 Kgs 25:27 לגלות; Ezek 1:2); Greek μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος ('deportation') is bureaucratic where the Hebrew is covenantal.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:11): ואחיו . . . בבל omitted in EF; יכניה] יכניא A; יאשיה] יאשיא A, יאשיהו EF.

verses.translation: Yekhonyah{H3204} begot{H3205} Shealtiel{H7597}; Shealtiel begot Zerubavel{H2216}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:12): mss ADG prefix ואחר גלות בבל ('and after the exile of Bavel'), as the Greek; Howard prints '(After the Babylonian exile)'. שאלתיאל (both)] שלתיאל A; יכניה] יכניא A.

verses.translation: Zerubavel{H2216} begot{H3205} Avihud{H31}, and Avihud begot —

greek_deviations: The base text drops three of the Greek's links here: Avihud begets Akim directly (v. 14), without Eliakim, Azor, or Zadok. Mss ABDEFG add אליקים אליקים הוליד את עזור after this verse, and DG open v. 14 with עזור הוליד את צדוק צדוק הוליד את — two stages of restoration toward the Greek chain, which Howard prints in parentheses.
translation_notes: The sentence runs over the verse-break: v. 13 ends with את and v. 14 opens with its object, אקים.
textual_notes: The ms writes זרובב״ל with the gershayim it uses for marked names.
Howard's apparatus (1:13): the second את] + אליקים אליקים הוליד את עזור ABDEFG; ואביהוד] אביהוד DG.

verses.translation: — Akim; and Akim begot{H3205} Elihud.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:14): DG prefix עזור הוליד את צדוק צדוק הוליד את ('Azor begot Zadok; Zadok begot'), completing the Greek chain; ואקים] אקים ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And Elihud begot{H3205} Elazar{H499}; and Elazar begot Mattan{H4977}; and Mattan begot Yaakov{H3290}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:15): ואליהוד] אליהוד ABDEFG; ואלעזר] אלעזר ABDEFG; ומתן] מתן ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And Yaakov{H3290} begot{H3205} Yoseph{H3130}. This is Yoseph, the husband{H376} of Miryam{H4813} — the one called{H7121} Mashiach{H4899}, and in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Christos.

one_way_hebrew: The scribe glosses the Hebrew משיח with the church's own word: ובלעז קריס״טוס — 'and in the foreign tongue, Christos' — marked as foreign by the gershayim, exactly like אוו״נגילי and אנטיק״ריסטוש at 24:14-15. A translator FROM Greek would have started from Χριστός and needed no gloss; the gloss runs the other way — the Hebrew word is native, the Greek word is the visitor.
greek_deviations: The base text lacks 'of whom was born Jesus' (Greek ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς): the sentence runs 'This is Yoseph, the husband of Miryam, the one called Mashiach.' Mss ABCDEFG ease it by adding אם ישו ('the mother of Yeshu') after Miryam, and Howard prints '(the mother of Jesus)' in parentheses.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:16): מרים] + אם ישו ABCDEFG; ובלעז] בלעז A, לעז DEFG; קריסטוס] קרישטוש ABDFG.

verses.translation: (So all{H3605} the generations{H8435} from Avraham{H85} to David{H1732} are fourteen generations; and from David to the exile{H1546} of Bavel{H894}, fourteen generations; and from the exile of Bavel to Yeshua{H3442}, fourteen generations.)

greek_deviations: The three-fourteens summary — the organizing device of Greek Matthew's genealogy — is absent from the base ms and most of the Shem Tov family. Howard's apparatus: 'Vs. 17 found only in mss DG.' He prints the verse (and the opening of v. 18) in parentheses. The base genealogy, which omits kings the count needs (vv. 9, 13-14), never counted fourteens at all: the count entered with the verse.
textual_notes: Printed in parentheses in Howard's text; the ms writes the numeral as י״ד (letter-numerals, 14).
Howard's apparatus (1:17): Vs. 17 found only in mss DG.

verses.translation: (And the birth{H3205} of Yeshua{H3442} was in this{H2088} manner{H655}:) And it came to pass{H1961}, when his mother{H517} was betrothed{H781} to Yoseph{H3130}, before{H6924} he knew{H3045} her, she was found{H4672} pregnant from the Spirit{H7307} of Holiness{H6944}.

one_way_hebrew: ארוסה — the Torah's own legal category (Deut 22:23-27, the betrothed נערה): Yoseph's dilemma in v. 19 is the case-law of that very passage. Greek μνηστευθείσης translates the legal term without its statute.
translation_notes: The opening clause ולידת מיש״ו היה בזה האופן belongs, with v. 17, to the DG supplement; Howard's parenthesis closes after האופן. The base ms text resumes at ויהי כאשר.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק שני (Perek 2) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (1:18): ולידת . . . האופן] found only in mss DG; מישו] ישו G; ארוסה] מאורסה A.

verses.translation: And Yoseph{H3130} was a righteous{H6662} man{H376}, and he did not wish{H7521} to dwell{H3427} with her — yet not to expose her{H1540}, to bring her{H935} to shame{H955}, nor to bind her over{H631} to death{H4194}; rather he wished to cover{H3680} over her.

one_way_hebrew: לכסות עליה — 'to cover over her': Prov 10:12's verb, ועל כל פשעים תכסה אהבה ('love covers all transgressions'). The righteous man's mercy is stated in Proverbs' own word.

The verse walks through Deut 22's betrothal case-law: the betrothed woman found with child faces public process (לגלותה, exposure) or death (למות, Deut 22:23-24); Yoseph declines both. Greek 'not willing to make her a public example' keeps the outline but loses the statute's terms — לאוסרה למות, 'to bind her over to death,' is court language (אסר, as at 24:9).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:19): איש] אישה ABDEFGH ('husband of'); צדיק היה] transposed in AH.

verses.translation: And as he thought{H2803} on this matter{H1697} in his heart{H3820}, behold{H2009}, a messenger{H4397} appeared{H7200} to him in a dream{H2472} and said{H559}: Yoseph{H3130}, son{H1121} of David{H1732}, do not fear{H3372} to take{H3947} Miryam{H4813} your wife{H802}, for she is pregnant from the Spirit{H7307} of Holiness{H6944}.

one_way_hebrew: אל תירא — the patriarchal reassurance formula (Gen 15:1 to Avraham; 26:24 to Yitschaq; 46:3 to Yaakov — on the way down to Egypt), spoken to 'Yoseph son of David' as to the fathers.
חלום — this Yoseph, like Genesis's Yoseph, receives revelation by dream and will carry the child down to Egypt (2:13); the Hebrew reader sees the first Yoseph behind the second at every step.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:20): והנה] הנה ABEFG; ואמר] לאמור BCDEFG; אליו omitted in A.

verses.translation: And she will bear{H3205} a son{H1121}, and you shall call{H7121} his name{H8034} Yeshua{H3442}, for he will save{H3467} my people{H5971} from their iniquities{H5771}.

one_way_hebrew: THE NAME-VERSE ONLY WORKS IN HEBREW: ותקרא שמו ישו״ע כי הוא יושיע — 'call his name YESHUA, for he YOSHIA (will save)' — name and verb are one root, ישע (H3467). Greek Ἰησοῦς... σώσει breaks the pun, and the reason-clause explains nothing to a Greek reader. The naming-formula with its built-in wordplay is the Bible's own (Gen 16:11 ישמעאל... כי שמע; Isa 7:14): the verse is native Hebrew, and Greek Matthew is its translation.
And here — precisely where the wordplay is explicit — the ms writes the name out in full, ישו״ע, instead of its usual abbreviation יש״ו (so again at 1:25). The scribe knew what the verse does.
greek_deviations: עמי — 'MY people' (the messenger speaks for the owner of the people), and מעונותם — 'their INIQUITIES' (עון, the weight-bearing covenant word of Exod 34:7, נשא עון), where Greek has ἁμαρτιῶν ('sins'). Ms A reads עמו ('his people') and מעונותיו.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:21): עמי] עמו A; מעונותם] מעונותיו A.

verses.translation: All{H3605} this{H2088} was to complete{H1584} what was written{H3789} from the prophet{H5030} by the mouth{H6310} of YHWH{H3068}:

one_way_hebrew: לגמור (H1584) — 'to complete, bring to full measure' (Ps 57:3, לאל גמר עלי — 'El who completes for me'): a native fulfillment idiom, one of several this text uses (לקיים, נשלם, להשלים) where Greek has the single πληρόω. A translator from Greek would render one verb one way; a Hebrew author varies as living writers do.

על פי ה״ — 'by the mouth of YHWH': the Torah's own idiom of command and word (Num 3:16, על פי יהוה). The Hebrew states where prophecy comes from — written from the prophet, spoken from the mouth of YHWH.
textual_notes: First occurrence in this chapter: the ms writes the Name as ה״ ('The Name', the reverent circumlocution), rendered YHWH throughout.
Howard's apparatus (1:22): ה״] השם G ('HaShem', written out); mss AB read על פי הנביא ה' ('by the mouth of the prophet of YHWH').

verses.translation: Behold{H2009}, the young woman{H5959} is with child{H2030} and will bear{H3205} a son{H1121}, and she shall call{H7121} his name{H8034} Immanuel{H6005} — that is to say, Elohim{H430} with us{H5973}.

one_way_hebrew: The quotation is Isa 7:14 in Isaiah's own consonants: הנה העלמה הרה... וקראת שמו עמנואל — with העלמה ('the young woman') and וקראת ('SHE shall call'), exactly as the Hebrew of Isaiah reads. Greek Matthew follows the LXX (παρθένος, 'virgin'; καλέσουσιν, 'they shall call'). A Hebrew author quotes his own Bible; a back-translator from Greek would have reproduced the LXX's readings. The Shem Tov text and the Hebrew Isaiah are one.

שר״ל — the scribal abbreviation of שרוצה לומר ('which means'), introducing the name's translation עמנו אלקים. Greek Matthew must gloss the name too (μεθερμηνευόμενον) — but it glosses a HEBREW name for Greek readers; this text glosses it in Hebrew shorthand for Hebrew readers.
textual_notes: First occurrence in this chapter: the ms writes אלקים — the reverent ק-spelling of אלהים — throughout.
Howard's apparatus (1:23): אלקים] אלים A.

verses.translation: And Yoseph{H3130} awoke{H3364} from his sleep{H8142} and did{H6213} according to all{H3605} that the messenger{H4397} of YHWH{H3068} commanded{H6680} him, and he took{H3947} his wife{H802}.

one_way_hebrew: ויעש ככל אשר צוה — the Torah's obedience formula, verbatim: ויעש נח ככל אשר צוה אתו אלהים (Gen 6:22); so of Moshe at the Tabernacle (Exod 40:16). Yoseph obeys in the exact sentence-shape of Noach and Moshe; Greek ἐποίησεν ὡς προσέταξεν translates the formula without its lineage.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:24): ה״] אלוהים G; מלאך ה״] המלאך F; יוסף omitted in G.

verses.translation: And he did not know{H3045} her until{H5704} she bore{H3205} her firstborn{H1060} son{H1121}; and he called{H7121} his name{H8034} Yeshua{H3442}.

one_way_hebrew: The ms writes the name in full again — ישו״ע — at the act of naming itself, as at v. 21: the full spelling appears exactly where the name is being conferred and explained.
greek_deviations: בנה הבכור — 'her FIRSTBORN son': the fuller reading (as in the KJV's Greek), where the oldest Greek copies (א B) have only 'a son.' The whole Shem Tov family carries הבכור — no variant is recorded.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (1:25): את omitted in BDEFG.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 1 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is a Hebrew genealogy, not a translated one. (1) 1:21 is the keystone: 'you shall call his name ישו״ע for he יושיע (will save)' — name and verb share the root ישע, a wordplay Greek Ἰησοῦς/σώσει cannot carry; the ms, which abbreviates the name יש״ו everywhere else, spells it out in full (ישו״ע) exactly at 1:21 and 1:25 where the naming is explicit. (2) 1:23 quotes Isa 7:14 as the Hebrew Bible reads it — העלמה ('the young woman'), וקראת ('SHE shall call') — where Greek Matthew follows the LXX (παρθένος, 'they shall call'): the text quotes Isaiah, not a retro-translation of Greek Matthew's LXX quotation. (3) The fourteen-count of 1:17 is found only in mss DG (Howard prints it in parentheses); the base genealogy omits Jotham and Ahaz (1:9) and Eliakim-Azor-Zadok (1:13-14) — it never counted fourteens; later mss patch the list toward the Greek. (4) 1:16 lacks 'of whom was born Jesus'; the scribe glosses משיח with ובלעז קריס״טוס — the church's word marked as the foreign one (as at 24:14-15). (5) 1:5 keeps Joshua's epithet רחב הזונה (Josh 6:25), dropped by all other mss. (6) 1:19 runs Yoseph's choice through Deut 22's betrothal case-law (exposure or death), and he chooses Prov 10:12's לכסות ('love covers'). (7) 1:22 'written from the prophet by the mouth of YHWH' (על פי ה״); the ms writes ה״ for the Name and אלקים with the reverent ק. (8) 1:24 obeys in Gen 6:22's formula; 1:25 keeps 'her firstborn son' with the fuller text-tradition. Fulfillment verbs vary natively (לגמור here; לקיים, נשלם elsewhere) against Greek's single πληρόω. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at v. 1 (Perek 1) and v. 18 (Perek 2).
